items.title: California's Filing Deadline
items.desc: Most injury claims in California must be filed within 2 years of the incident, though claims against a government entity can require notice in as little as 6 months. Waiting too long can cost you the right to recover anything at all.

items.title: Fault Doesn't Have to Be All-or-Nothing
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault, meaning you can still recover damages even if you were partly responsible for the crash. Your compensation is simply reduced by your share of fault, not eliminated.

items.title: No Cap on Pain and Suffering
items.desc: In ordinary injury cases, California places no cap on non-economic damages like pain and suffering. We can help you understand what that might mean for your specific situation.

items.title: You Pay Nothing Upfront
items.desc: We work on contingency, so there's no fee unless we secure a recovery for you. That means getting legal help doesn't add financial stress while you're already dealing with an injury.

items.question: How long do I have to file a personal injury claim in California?
items.answer: Generally, you have 2 years from the date of the incident to file most personal injury claims in California. If a government entity is involved, that window can shrink to as little as 6 months, so it's worth checking sooner rather than later.

items.question: What if I was partly at fault for the accident?
items.answer: California uses a pure comparative fault rule, so being partially at fault doesn't bar you from recovering compensation. Your final recovery is just reduced by your percentage of fault, which we can help evaluate.

items.question: Where do crashes tend to happen in Dunsmuir?
items.answer: Public collision records show higher counts along I-5, Dunsmuir Avenue, and Castle Avenue, with reports clustering on Saturdays between 6 and 8 p.m. These are simply reported counts, not a judgment about any particular road or area.

items.question: Are you a law firm?
items.answer: We are a personal injury team that helps injured people in Dunsmuir and Siskiyou County understand their options and pursue claims for compensation. We work directly with clients on a contingency basis.

items.question: How much does it cost to contact you?
items.answer: Contacting us costs nothing, and we work on contingency. That means you typically pay no fee unless we recover compensation on your behalf.
